title: NEOWISE 2019-2024 data agree with the dated dust maxima of WR 125, WR 137 and HD 36402 from Williams (2019) and show new dust episodes in WR 47c and WR 75-11 and a 3.5-year cycle in WR 75-27
abstract: Question: did the Wolf-Rayet (WR) dust-variability results of Williams (2019), from NEOWISE 2014-2018, predict the 2019-2024 NEOWISE data, and do other Galactic WR stars show new infrared variability? Method: WISE 2010 and NEOWISE 2014-2024 W1/W2 visit light curves of the 718 stars of the Galactic WR catalogue v1.36 and two LMC stars, with 1,058 magnitude-matched isolated field stars as an empirical null. Per star: chi-square with an empirical error floor, a drop-one-visit test, the von Neumann ratio, the colour of the varying flux and a centroid test. We applied the same classes to the controls, and we compared each variable with up to five local field stars in the same frames. Results: dated maxima held for WR 125 (observed 2020.75, predicted 2021.0), WR 137 (2023.35 vs 2023.05) and HD 36402 (2021.41 vs 2021.13; template rho 0.96, p = 1e-4; refitted P = 4.99 +- 0.01 yr). WR 19, WR 91-1 and HD 38030 faded without a new rise. The 1.49-yr period of WR 46-7 predicted the new data (rho 0.68, p = 0.01). The 0.758-yr period of WR 60-4 failed (0.700 yr or the 1.75-yr alias fits). Tests of saturated stars (WR 70, WR 77t) were not decisive. WR 47c had a new 0.40-mag dust episode with a maximum near 2022.1 (12-17 yr after the previous one). WR 75-11 brightened by 0.47 mag from 2021.6 to 2024.2 and was still rising. The WC8 star WR 75-27 (VVV CL074-2) changes by 2.5 mag at 4.6 um with a quasi-period of 3.5 yr (maxima 2015.5, 2018.6, 2022.2), and it is redder when brighter (varying flux near 500-650 K). This agrees with periodic dust formation in an eccentric binary, but a blended dusty AGB star within 1 arcsec is not excluded. The next maximum is expected near 2025.7. Of 416 unsaturated WR stars, 9 show coherent changes that are redder when brighter, against 4.3 expected from controls (p = 0.031). New candidates are WR 75-9, WR 76-1, WR 111-11 and WR 111-5. Local field stars do not share these changes (local trends at most 0.18 mag). Saturated NEOWISE photometry (W2 < 6.5) has error floors of 0.1-0.4 mag and AllWISE-to-NEOWISE offsets up to 1.4 mag, which explains the apparent rise of AG Car. Limitations: 6-arcsec resolution and crowding remove 179 catalogue stars; saturation limits the bright dust makers; no spectra; class thresholds are rule-based.
